clue.text: A meal's been cooked for sailors

indicators.note: food that is cooked is worked over, so these letters are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's galley has produced a meal for the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals an anagram of A MEALS BEEN, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Able seamen are the ordinary qualified ratings of a navy or merchant crew, hence sailors.

clue.text: You do what you like with it

definitions.text: You do what you like with it

parts.words: You do what you like with it
parts.note: read as a riddle: the faculty of choosing for oneself is what lets anyone act as they please

explanation.definitionFit: The power to choose one's own actions unconstrained is exactly what lets a person act as they wish.

clue.text: New praise for old Iran

indicators.note: a new version of the word praise is a fresh arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone offers fresh compliments to the Iran of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the country's name in the West until 1935, when it became officially known as Iran.

clue.text: Firm work with the pen

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A company does its business with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is an enclosure for keeping poultry, a pen in the farmyard sense.

clue.text: These heavyweights experienced harrowing times

parts.note: harrowing means distressing but also dragging a harrow over fields, the job of big farm horses

explanation.surface: Heavyweight boxers have been through a dreadful ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: A harrow is a farm implement that breaks up soil; heavy draught horses once pulled it.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught horses are the massive breeds that pulled carts and ploughs, the heavyweights of the farm.

clue.text: A figure of speech satisfied a figure in speech

parts.note: to have met a need or demand is to have satisfied it

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the number word is pronounced like the ending spelt P-H-O-R

parts.note: four is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A figure of speech pleased a figure appearing in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says the number is heard, not spelt: FOUR sounds like PHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a rhetorical device describing one thing as another, a classic figure of speech.

clue.text: Foreign Office has its back to the wall

definitions.meaning: the French word for an office, taken into English

definitions.text: has its back to the wall
definitions.meaning: a writing desk with drawers, which normally stands against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: Bureau is French for office and in Britain also names a writing desk that stands against a wall.

clue.text: One among the lesser folk, historically

definitions.text: One among the lesser folk, historically

indicators.note: the letters sit among those of the words lesser folk, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone belonged to the lower orders in times past.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval peasant bound to the land was one of the lowest classes in feudal society.

clue.text: A lone crab scuttles round by the sea in Spain

indicators.note: a crab scuttling round moves about, so the letters of the phrase move into a new order

explanation.surface: A solitary crab scurries about on a Spanish beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the Catalan port city on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Key duet composition

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters of duet are put together afresh

explanation.surface: An important piece written for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a short musical study, a composition written to practise technique.

clue.text: Quits at university levels

parts.note: being quits with someone means being square, or evens
UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their studies at the higher levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' looks like the verb for leaving but is the adjective meaning square.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up a score or surface is to make it level, so the phrase means levels as a verb.

clue.text: One of many carried by a caddy

definitions.text: One of many carried by a caddy

parts.words: One of many carried by a caddy
parts.note: a caddy is a golfer's bag carrier but also a small tin for storing tea

explanation.walkthrough: The golf caddie leads the surface; the tea caddy gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a container holding many dried leaves of tea.

clue.text: Show girl without sex appeal?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
IT is the crossword's old slang for sex appeal

explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage musical about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Not a big audience — it was for charity

definitions.meaning: in theatre talk a thin audience is a bad turnout for the night
a workhouse where paupers were given shelter at public expense

explanation.definitionFit: A poorhouse was a public institution housing the destitute, and a poor house is a small theatre crowd.

clue.text: It's not all bias

parts.note: the clue plays on partial meaning both not complete and prejudiced

explanation.walkthrough: Partial means incomplete (not all) as well as biased, so the word is both readings at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Partiality is an unfair preference for one side, which is bias.

clue.text: Seer?

parts.note: a seer is a prophet, but read literally it is simply one who sees something happen

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saw an event take place and can testify to it is literally one who sees.

clue.text: Church parade is just part of it

definitions.text: Church parade is just part of it

parts.words: Church parade is just part of it
parts.note: a church parade is when troops march to a religious service, one duty of soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: Time spent serving in the armed forces includes parades of troops to church services.

clue.text: High romance?

parts.note: high can mean tall, and a romance is a story; an exaggerated story is the result

explanation.walkthrough: TALL is high and TALE is a romance, so the two words make the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlikely, exaggerated story is a fanciful romance in the old sense of an adventure narrative.

clue.text: Fashionably tailored, he's concerned with his image

indicators.note: fashioning means shaping anew, so the letters of tailored are refashioned

explanation.surface: A man in a smart suit cares about how he looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The image is an idol, not his appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships a graven image, so his religion is centred on it.

clue.text: Small gimmicky articles — book matches, for example?

parts.note: a novel is a book
ties are matches between teams, as in cup ties

explanation.surface: Little gimmicks such as matchbooks are on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Book matches look like one item, matchbooks; split them. Cup ties are knockout matches in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelties are cheap little trinkets or gadgets sold for amusement.

clue.text: Confirm if the light goes out

indicators.note: the flare's name goes outside, wrapping round the little word if

parts.note: a Very light is a signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: Check whether the lamp has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' seems to say the light is extinguished; it means the flare's name wraps round IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify something is to establish that it is true, to confirm it.

clue.text: No, I am wrong; she was Ruth's mother-in-law

indicators.note: the words are put together wrongly, so their letters must be reordered

explanation.surface: A woman denies an identity and names her famous relative.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament Book of Ruth, Ruth stays loyal to her husband's mother Naomi.

clue.text: Being annoyed, informed the police

definitions.meaning: British slang for irritated or put out
a nark is a police informer, so to nark is to grass to the police

explanation.definitionFit: Narked is British slang for irritated, and to nark is to act as a police informer.

clue.text: Master takes female, 50, in marriage

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
Rita is a woman's name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A master marries a woman of fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital describes things relating to marriage, as in marital bliss.

clue.text: High light, low point

parts.note: a low is the sound a cow makes, a moo
N is the north point of the compass

explanation.surface: A best moment and a worst moment set side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like the opposite of high but is a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is a light seen high in the night sky.

clue.text: Something so cheap as to rule out profit?

parts.note: to bar something is to exclude or rule it out
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Something priced so low that the seller makes no money.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an item bought for less than its value, so it is surprisingly cheap.

clue.text: Note edge of radar echo

parts.note: B is a musical note
a lip is an edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: Someone notices the rim of a radar return.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is the small spot of light on a radar screen marking an object detected.

clue.text: Refuse organic food?

definitions.meaning: waste matter, rubbish, especially from butchering
a playful reading: food made of organs such as liver and kidneys

explanation.definitionFit: Offal is a carcass's edible organs and, originally, the waste parts thrown away.

clue.text: Banality means one looks for new interests

indicators.note: a new form of the word interests is its letters in fresh order

explanation.surface: Boredom leads a person to seek new hobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: Triteness is the quality of being stale and overused, which is banality.
